newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL STAY CLEAR AS BARCELONA RETAKE SECOND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL STAY CLEAR AS BARCELONA RETAKE SECOND.

text.p: Barcelona regained second place in the Spanish first division on goal difference from Real Betis on Sunday with an emphatic 4-0 victory over struggling Sevilla.
But Real Madrid maintained their nine-point lead over both sides thanks to two first half goals by Fernando Hierro in a straightforward 2-0 home win over Zaragoza.
Holders Atletico Madrid stay in fifth after a last-gasp win at Rayo Vallecano.
Betis had beaten Oviedo 4-0 on Saturday, leaving Barcelona needing to win by two goals to retake second place.
The Catalans romped to victory after a goalless first half and could easily have scored eight as Ronaldo, Juan Pizzi, Luis Enrique Martinez and Oscar Garcia found the target.
Ronaldo's goal was his 23rd of the season, leaving him one ahead of Betis' Alfonso Perez in the Spanish goalscoring tables.

However with just 12 games left to play Barcelona are running out of time to catch leaders Real, who played a fine first half and then shut up shop and were happy to defend their lead after the break.
"We're playing well, we have our style of playing which is producing dividends," said double goalscorer Hierro.
Fourth-placed Deportivo Coruna are a further three points behind Barcelona and Betis thanks to a 2-1 home win over Racing Santander.
The game was marked by a fine performance by striker Renaldo who scored the winning goal on a poor day for fellow Brazilian, playmaker Rivaldo.
Deportivo stay seven points ahead of Atletico after last year's league and cup double winners came within a whisker of losing their fifth consecutive game.

But Atletico turned a threatened 1-0 defeat into a 2-1 victory in the last five minutes of their game at Rayo with a goal from a corner by Daniel Prodan and a controversial penalty converted by Milinko Pantic.
"It was a bit like a Five Nations rugby international," joked Atletico striker Kiko Narvaez after the game, in which Atletico had been outplayed by struggling Rayo.

Juan Eduardo Esnaider was left out of the Atletico squad for the game. The fiery Argentine striker missed a penalty and several other chances in Wednesday's epic European Cup defeat by Ajax and insulted coach Radomir Antic after being substituted.
